p.src: As they drew close to the woods, twenty or thirty great gongs suddenly clanged out all at once. The stockade soldiers were thrown into confusion and wanted only to flee. Huang Xin shouted, “Hold! All of you, form ranks for me!” Then he called, “Warden Liu, guard the prison carts.” Liu Gao, sitting on his horse, could not even manage a reply; he merely muttered, “Heavenly Lord who rescues from suffering and calamity.” He vowed to sponsor a hundred thousand copies of the scriptures and three hundred temples if only he might be saved. His frightened face looked like a bewitched winter melon, turning green one moment and yellow the next. Huang Xin was a military officer and did possess some courage. Spurring his horse forward to investigate, he saw three to five hundred bandit underlings pour out around the woods in orderly ranks. Every one of them was tall and strong, with a fierce face and savage eyes; red kerchiefs wrapped their heads, quilted jackets covered their bodies, sharp swords hung at their waists, and long spears filled their hands. They had already surrounded the entire party. Three heroes leaped from the woods—one dressed in blue, one in green, and one in red. Each wore a headscarf patterned with gilded swastikas, carried a saber at his waist, and brandished a broad-bladed polearm as he barred the road. In the center stood Yan Shun, the “Brocade-Furred Tiger”; on his right was Wang Ying, the “Stumpy Tiger”; and on his left was Zheng Tianshou, the “Fair-Faced Gentleman.” The three heroes roared, “Travelers who reach this place must halt! Leave three thousand strings of gold as road money, and you may pass freely.” Huang Xin shouted from his horse, “You rogues, mind your manners! The ‘Guardian of the Three Mountains’ is here!” The three heroes glared and shouted, “Even if you are the ‘Guardian of the Three Mountains,’ you must still pay three thousand taels of gold for passage! If you do not have it, we will not let you pass.” Huang Xin said, “I am a military commissioner carrying out official business for my superiors. What road money would I have for you?” The three heroes laughed. “Never mind that you are merely a commissioner in the service of your superiors—even if His Majesty the Emperor were passing through, he too would have to pay three thousand strings in road money. If you do not have it, leave the officials here as security while you go fetch the money to ransom them.” Huang Xin flew into a rage and cursed, “You brigands! How dare you be so insolent!” He ordered the men on either side to beat the drums and sound the gongs. Huang Xin spurred his horse, flourished his sword, and charged straight at Yan Shun. All three heroes raised their polearms and came together to fight Huang Xin. When Huang Xin saw all three heroes closing upon him, he fought with all his strength from horseback for ten rounds—but how could he withstand the three of them? Moreover, Liu Gao was a civil official and could not advance to help. Seeing how matters stood, he wanted only to flee. Huang Xin feared that capture by the three would ruin his reputation. With no other choice, he wheeled his horse and went thundering back along the road they had come, while the three chieftains pursued him with polearms raised. Huang Xin could spare no thought for the others; alone, he galloped back to Qingfeng Town. When the soldiers saw Huang Xin turn his horse, they raised a great cry, abandoned the prison carts, and scattered in every direction. Only Liu Gao remained. Seeing that the situation was dire, he hurriedly reined his horse around and lashed it three times in succession; but just as the horse was about to run, the underlings pulled up a trip rope, overturning Liu Gao’s mount and hurling him headlong to the ground. The underlings surged forward as one, seized Liu Gao, and took the prison carts. They broke open the carts; Hua Rong had already forced open his own, leaped out, and snapped all his bonds. He then smashed the other prison cart and rescued Song Jiang. Several underlings bound Liu Gao’s hands behind his back, went forward to seize the horse he had ridden, and also took the three horses that had drawn the carts. They stripped Liu Gao’s clothes from him and gave them to Song Jiang to wear, then sent the horses up the mountain ahead of them. The three heroes, together with Hua Rong and the underlings, bound the naked Liu Gao and escorted him back to the mountain stronghold.

p.src: By the time they climbed the mountain that night, it was already the second watch, and they all assembled in the Hall of Righteousness. Song Jiang and Hua Rong were invited to sit in the places of honor, while the three heroes sat opposite to keep them company, and food and wine were prepared for their entertainment. Yan Shun ordered the lads to go and drink among themselves. In the hall Hua Rong thanked the three heroes, saying, “My elder brother and I both owe our lives to you three brave men, and through you our wrongs have been avenged. Such a debt is hard to repay. But my wife, child, and younger sister are still in Qingfeng Stockade. Huang Xin is certain to seize them. How can they be rescued?” Yan Shun said, “Set your mind at ease, Warden Hua. Huang Xin will surely not dare to arrest your honorable wife at once. Even if he does seize her, they will have to pass along this road. Tomorrow, we three brothers will go down the mountain and bring your honorable wife and younger sister back to you.” He then sent underlings down the mountain to investigate in advance. Hua Rong thanked him, saying, “I am deeply grateful for your great kindness, brave sir.” Song Jiang then said, “Now bring that scoundrel Liu Gao before me.” Yan Shun said, “Tie him to the general’s pillar, cut open his belly, and take out his heart to celebrate our elder brother’s good fortune.” Hua Rong said, “I will cut down this scoundrel with my own hand.” Song Jiang cursed him: “You scoundrel! I bore you no grievance in former days and hold no feud against you now. Why did you believe that wicked woman and seek to harm me? Now that you have been captured, what defense can you offer?” Hua Rong said, “Brother, why bother questioning him?” He thrust his knife into Liu Gao’s chest and, with a single scoop, cut out his heart, which he presented before Song Jiang. The underlings dragged the corpse aside. Song Jiang said, “Though today we have killed this vile slanderer, that wanton woman is still alive, so I have not yet vented the full measure of my anger.” Wang the Stumpy Tiger said, “Set your mind at ease, brother. Tomorrow I will go down the mountain myself and seize that woman. This time, let me have her for my pleasure.” Everyone burst into laughter. When the night’s drinking was over, each retired to rest. When they rose the next day, they discussed the attack on Qingfeng Stockade. Yan Shun said, “The lads exhausted themselves running yesterday. Let them rest for a day today. It will not be too late to descend the mountain early tomorrow.” Song Jiang said, “That is reasonable. We should indeed recuperate until our men are vigorous and our horses strong; there is no need to hurry.”

p.src: Leaving aside the mountain stronghold as it mustered its troops and prepared to depart, let us tell how Commandant Huang Xin galloped alone back to the main fort at Qingfeng Town, mustered its soldiers and horsemen, and placed every palisade gate under close guard. Huang Xin wrote an urgent report and ordered two drill captains to ride with all speed and deliver it to Prefect Murong. On hearing that an urgent military dispatch had arrived, the prefect convened court that very night and read Huang Xin's report: Hua Rong had rebelled and joined forces with the bandits of Mount Qingfeng; Qingfeng Fort might fall at any moment; the danger was grave, and a capable commander must be sent at once to defend the district. The prefect was greatly alarmed. He immediately sent for Qin Ming, commander of Qingzhou's troops under the Military Command Commission, to come at once and confer on this grave military matter. This man came from Kaizhou north of the mountains. His surname was Qin and his given name Ming. Because he was hot-tempered and his voice rang like thunder, everyone called him Qin Ming, the Thunderbolt. He came from a family of military officers, wielded a great wolf-toothed mace, and possessed the valor to withstand ten thousand men. When Qin Ming heard that the prefect had summoned him, he went straight to the prefectural offices. He and the prefect exchanged courtesies. Prefect Murong produced Huang Xin's urgent report and gave it to Commander Qin to read. Qin Ming flew into a rage. “How dare that red-headed wretch behave so outrageously! Your Excellency need not worry. I shall muster the troops at once, and if I fail to capture this villain, I swear never to appear before you again!” Prefect Murong said, “If you delay, General, I fear those fellows will attack Qingfeng Fort.” Qin Ming replied, “How could I dare delay such a matter? This very night I shall muster the men and horses, and we shall set out early tomorrow.” The prefect was delighted and promptly ordered wine, meat, and rations prepared and sent outside the city in readiness for the troops. Enraged by the news that Hua Rong had rebelled, Qin Ming mounted his horse and hurried to the Military Command Commission. There he mustered one hundred cavalry and four hundred infantry, sent them outside the city to assemble, and made ready to depart.

I have come expressly to arrest you. If you understand your position, dismount and submit to bonds, and spare me from bloodying my hands and soiling my feet.”
Hua Rong replied with a conciliatory smile, “Commander, please hear my explanation. How could one as insignificant as Hua Rong ever willingly rebel against the court?

In truth, that scoundrel Liu Gao fabricated charges from nothing and used public authority to avenge a private grudge. He drove me to where I could neither return home nor seek refuge in my country, so for the time being I have hidden here. I beg you, Commander, to investigate carefully and deliver me from this plight.”
Qin Ming said, “You still refuse to dismount and submit to bonds—what are you waiting for?
Instead, you persist in glib deception to unsettle the army's resolve.”
He shouted for the drums on both wings to sound.
Qin Ming swung his wolf-toothed mace and charged straight at Hua Rong.
Hua Rong laughed loudly. “Qin Ming, you truly cannot recognize when an honorable man is showing you mercy.
I treated you with respect because you are my superior officer, and you took it for genuine fear!”
He spurred his horse, leveled his spear, and rode out to fight Qin Ming.
The two clashed beneath Mount Qingfeng. Truly, when matched players meet at chess, neither can rely on luck; when a great general encounters a worthy foe, he may display his finest skill.
As these two generals tested their prowess, behold:

p.src: Qin Ming and Hua Rong now crossed weapons and fought for forty or fifty bouts without either gaining the upper hand. After many more bouts, Hua Rong feigned an opening, wheeled his horse, and fled down a narrow path beneath the mountain. Qin Ming flew into a rage and gave chase. Hua Rong secured his spear by its ring, reined his horse to a halt, raised his bow in his left hand, and drew an arrow with his right. Pulling the bow to the full, he twisted around and loosed a single shaft at the crest of Qin Ming's helmet. It struck squarely and shot away the great red tassel, as though merely sending him a warning. Qin Ming started in alarm and dared pursue no farther. He abruptly wheeled his horse and was just about to resume the attack when all the bandits rushed noisily back up the mountain. Hua Rong took another path and likewise returned to the mountain stronghold.

p.src: By then dusk was falling, and both men and horses were exhausted from the march; when at last they reached the foot of the mountain and were about to pitch camp and cook, torches flared wildly above and gongs and drums sounded in confusion. Qin Ming's anger flared anew, and he led forty or fifty cavalrymen charging up the mountain. A shower of arrows came down from the woods above and wounded several more soldiers. Qin Ming had no choice but to turn back down the mountain and tell his men to carry on cooking. They had barely kindled their fires when eighty or ninety torches appeared on the mountain and came sweeping down amid whoops and whistles. But just as Qin Ming hastened to lead his men in pursuit, all the torches went out at once. Though there was moonlight that night, dark clouds veiled it, leaving the scene dim. Unable to contain his fury, Qin Ming ordered the soldiers to light torches and burn the trees. Just then, drums and flutes sounded from a spur of the mountain. When Qin Ming galloped up to look, he saw more than ten torches burning on the summit, illuminating Hua Rong as he attended Song Jiang while they drank. At the sight, Qin Ming had nowhere to vent his rage. Reining in below the mountain, he hurled abuse upward. Hua Rong called back, “Commander Qin, there is no need to be so vexed. Go back and rest for now. Tomorrow you and I shall fight until one of us is dead and settle the victory once and for all.” Qin Ming shouted, “You rebel! Come down here, and I shall fight you for three hundred bouts this very moment. We can settle all else afterward.” Hua Rong laughed. “Commander Qin, you are weary today. Even if I defeated you, it would be no proof of prowess. Go back for now and return tomorrow.” Qin Ming grew still more furious and kept cursing from below. He wanted to find a way up but feared Hua Rong's bow, and so remained on the lower slope shouting abuse. While he was still shouting curses, a cry suddenly arose from the troops under his command. Qin Ming hurried back down and saw firebombs and flaming arrows pouring from the mountain on that side. Behind them, groups of twenty or thirty bandits fired bows and crossbows at the men from the darkness. The troops raised a great clamor and crowded together into a deep ravine on the far side of the mountain to take shelter. It was already around the third watch. Just as the troops thought themselves sheltered from the bolts, they cried out in misery: water came surging down from upstream, sweeping men and horses into the creek, where each struggled desperately for life. All who managed to climb ashore were caught with hooked poles by the bandits and taken alive up the mountain; all who could not reach the bank drowned in the creek. As for Qin Ming, his rage now soared to heaven and seemed ready to shatter his skull. Then he caught sight of a narrow path to one side. He wheeled his horse and charged up the mountain. Before he had gone thirty or fifty paces, horse and rider tumbled together into a concealed pit. Fifty men armed with hooked poles lay in ambush on either side. They hauled Qin Ming out, stripped him of his battle robe, clothing, armor, helmet, and weapons, then bound him with a rope. They rescued his horse as well and escorted them both up to Qingfeng Mountain.

p.src: The band of lesser outlaws brought Qin Ming up to the stronghold, and by then dawn had already broken. The five heroes sat in the Hall of Righteous Assembly, while the lesser outlaws led Qin Ming, bound fast, before them. At the sight of him, Hua Rong hurriedly sprang from his chair and came down from the hall. He personally untied Qin Ming, helped him inside, then bowed his head to the floor before him. Qin Ming hastily returned the courtesy and said, “I am your captive, and you may hack me to pieces if you wish. Why, then, do you bow to me?” Hua Rong knelt and said, “The lesser outlaws did not know your honored rank and unwittingly offended you. I earnestly beg your forgiveness.” He immediately fetched clothes for Qin Ming to put on. Qin Ming asked Hua Rong, “Who is this hero who sits at the head?” Hua Rong replied, “He is my elder brother, Song Jiang, Clerk Song of Yuncheng County. These three are the masters of this stronghold: Yan Shun, Wang Ying, and Zheng Tianshou.” Qin Ming said, “I already know these three. Can this Clerk Song be none other than Song Gongming of Shandong, known as the ‘Timely Rain’?” Song Jiang replied, “I am that humble man.” Qin Ming hurriedly bowed and said, “I have long heard your illustrious name. I never imagined I would meet so righteous a man today!” Song Jiang hastened to return the courtesy again and again. Noticing that Song Jiang had difficulty walking, Qin Ming asked, “Elder brother, how did you come to injure your honored leg?” Song Jiang then related the whole affair to Qin Ming, beginning with his departure from Yuncheng County and ending with the beating he had suffered at Commandant Liu’s hands. Qin Ming merely shook his head and said, “How much mischief is caused by listening to only one side of a story! Allow me to return to the prefecture and explain this matter to Prefect Murong.” Yan Shun urged him to remain for several days, then ordered cattle and horses slaughtered and a banquet prepared. The soldiers captured and brought up the mountain were all lodged in rooms behind the stronghold and likewise supplied with food and wine.

p.src: After drinking several cups, Qin Ming rose and said, “Gentlemen, since you have shown me such kindness and spared my life, return my armor, horse, and weapons and let me go back to the prefecture.” Yan Shun said, “You are mistaken, Commander. You led five hundred troops from Qingzhou, and they have all been lost. How can you return to the prefecture? How could Prefect Murong fail to hold you accountable? You would do better to remain for a while in our humble mountain stronghold. This is hardly a place worthy of stabling your horse, but if you joined us here, we would weigh out gold and silver in equal shares and provide complete suits of clothing. Would that not be better than suffering the arrogance of those grand official caps?” When Qin Ming heard this, he strode down from the hall and declared, “In life Qin Ming is a man of the Great Song, and in death he shall be a ghost of the Great Song. The court raised me to be Commander of Horse and Foot and also bestowed upon me the office of Military Controller. It has never wronged me. How could I consent to become an outlaw and rebel against the court? If you gentlemen mean to kill me, then kill me, but never imagine that I will submit and join you.” Hua Rong hurried after him, caught hold of him, and said, “Elder Brother Qin, calm your anger and hear me out. I too am the son of an official appointed by the court, but, having no other choice, I was driven to this pass. Since you are unwilling to become an outlaw, Commander, how could we force you to join us? Please sit a little longer. When the feast is over, I shall have your clothes, armor, helmet, saddled horse, and weapons returned and let you depart.” But Qin Ming refused to sit down. Hua Rong urged him again: “Commander, last night and today you have spent a full day and night in exhausting toil. Even a man can scarcely bear it; how could you depart without first letting that horse eat its fill?” Hearing this, Qin Ming reflected that Hua Rong was right. He returned to the hall, sat down, and resumed drinking. The five heroes took turns filling his cup, engaging him in conversation, and urging him to drink. Qin Ming was already weary and sore, and moreover could not withstand the heroes’ repeated urging. He drank freely until he was drunk, then was helped into a sleeping chamber and put to bed. The others then went about their business, of which nothing more need be said here.

p.src: Now Qin Ming slept soundly until the hour of the dragon the next morning. When he awoke, he sprang up, washed, and immediately prepared to descend the mountain. All the heroes came to detain him, saying, “Commander, at least eat breakfast before you leave. We shall escort you down the mountain.” But Qin Ming was an impatient man and insisted on going down at once. The others hurriedly prepared food and wine to entertain him. They brought out his helmet and armor and helped Qin Ming put them on, then led over his horse and brought his wolf-toothed mace. Having first ordered men to wait below the mountain, the five heroes escorted Qin Ming down, bade him farewell, and returned his horse and weapons. Qin Ming mounted, took up his wolf-toothed mace, and, as full daylight broke, left Mount Qingfeng and galloped along the road toward Qingzhou. After traveling ten li, around the hour of the snake, he saw clouds of smoke and dust rising wildly in the distance, while not a single traveler was on the road. At the sight, Qin Ming was already deeply suspicious. When he reached the outskirts of the city and looked about, he found that the several hundred households formerly there had all been burned to bare ground. Across the field of rubble lay countless murdered men and women, sprawled in every direction. Qin Ming was horrified. He spurred his horse across the ruins to the city wall and shouted for the gate to be opened, but saw that the drawbridge had been raised high, while soldiers, banners, rolling logs, and stones stood arrayed along the defenses. Qin Ming reined in his horse and shouted, “Lower the drawbridge and let me into the city!” Someone on the wall had already recognized Qin Ming, and at once the drums sounded and the soldiers raised a great clamor. Qin Ming cried, “I am Commander Qin! Why will you not let me into the city?” Then Prefect Murong appeared beside the battlements and thundered, “You rebel! Have you no sense of shame? Last night you led men and horses against the city, killed many innocent citizens, and burned down countless houses. Yet today you have the audacity to return and try to trick us into opening the gate. The imperial court has never treated you unjustly. How could a wretch like you commit such an inhuman deed? I have already sent a messenger to report the matter to the court. Sooner or later you will be captured, and then your body will be hacked into ten thousand pieces!” Qin Ming shouted, “Your Excellency is mistaken! I lost my men and horses and was then captured by those scoundrels and taken up the mountain. I have only just escaped. How could I possibly have attacked the city last night?” The prefect shouted, “How could I fail to recognize your horse, armor, weapons, and helmet? Everyone on the wall clearly saw you directing the red-headed men as they killed and set fires. How can you deny it? Even if you had been defeated and captured, how could not one of your five hundred soldiers have escaped to bring us word? You now hope to trick us into opening the gate so that you can seize your family, but your wife and the rest were all put to death this morning. If you do not believe me, I shall show you her head.” A soldier raised the severed head of Qin Ming’s wife on the point of a spear and showed it to him. Qin Ming was a hot-tempered man. At the sight of his wife’s head, rage nearly burst his chest. Unable to explain himself, he could only cry out at the cruel injustice. Crossbow bolts rained down from the wall, forcing Qin Ming to retreat. Across the fields he could still see flames that had not yet gone out. Qin Ming turned his horse back across the ruins, wishing only to find a place to die. After pondering for a long while, he spurred his horse and retraced his former road. He had gone scarcely another ten li when a band of mounted men emerged from the woods. At their head rode five heroes: none other than Song Jiang, Hua Rong, Yan Shun, Wang Ying, and Zheng Tianshou, followed by one or two hundred lesser bandits. Song Jiang leaned forward in his saddle and said, “Commander, why have you not returned to Qingzhou? p.src: Now Huang Xin, upon reaching Qingfeng Town, issued orders to its soldiers and civilians, mustered the garrison troops, and kept watch day and night. He held the stockade gates fast and dared not venture out to fight. Again and again he sent men to gather intelligence, but there was still no sign of troops coming from Qingzhou to support him. That day, a report suddenly came: “Commander Qin has arrived outside the stockade, alone on horseback, and is calling for the gate to be opened.” On hearing this, Huang Xin mounted at once and galloped to the gate to look. Sure enough, there was one man on one horse, without a single attendant. Huang Xin ordered the stockade gate opened and the drawbridge lowered, then welcomed Commander Qin inside. They rode straight to the public hall of the main stronghold, where they dismounted, and Huang Xin invited him into the hall. When they had exchanged courtesies, Huang Xin asked, “Commander, why have you come here alone on horseback?” Qin Ming first related how his troops and horses had been lost, and then said, “Song Gongming, the ‘Timely Rain’ of Shandong, is generous with his wealth and stands by justice. He befriends worthy heroes throughout the land—who does not admire him? He is now on Qingfeng Mountain, and this time I too have joined the stronghold. You have neither wife nor children, so why not heed my words and join us at the mountain stronghold? Then you will no longer have to suffer the arrogance of those civil officials.” Huang Xin replied, “Since my honored superior is there, how could I, Huang Xin, dare refuse to follow you? But I had never heard that Song Gongming was on the mountain. Why do you now say that the ‘Timely Rain’ Song Gongming is there? Where did he come from?” Qin Ming laughed. “He is none other than Zhang San, the ‘Yuncheng Tiger,’ whom you escorted away the other day. He feared that revealing his true name would bring his own criminal case to light, so he claimed only to be Zhang San.” Hearing this, Huang Xin stamped his foot and said, “Had I known that he was Song Gongming, I would have released him on the road myself. At the time I failed to see the truth and listened only to Liu Gao’s one-sided account. I very nearly cost him his life.” As Qin Ming and Huang Xin were discussing their departure in the public offices, a garrison soldier came to report: “Two bodies of troops are charging toward the town, beating gongs and pounding drums!” When Qin Ming and Huang Xin heard this, they both mounted their horses and went forward to meet the enemy. When they reached the stockade gate and looked out, they saw dust blotting out the sun and a murderous air veiling the sky.
